properties.content:

Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 8245726
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/20/2025
Comments: On August 20, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of EQT's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4014690 and violations issued for a 1-3 barrel release of a production fluid, frack chemical and fresh water mixture.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that had a different Operator's information posted on it. The Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues.At the time of this inspection, there appeared to be rain water puddles in the area of the previous release and scraping of contaminated gravel. The Department did not observe a sheen in any puddles of apparent rainwater in the release area. The Department did not observe the trench previously observed to be bordering the secondary containment in the release area during IR 4014690. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the release area and collected the following soil conductivity readings: 0.75mS, 0.48mS, and 0.44mS . These readings were found to be comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.67mS.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at thus time pending the Act 2 Final report submittal, receipt, review, and approval by the Department's Environmental Cleanup and Brownfield Program.

Violation Code: 78a65(e) - SITE RESTORATION – Post drilling restoration reports – Operator failed to submit a restoration report to the Department within 60 calendar days after post drilling restoration under 25 Pa. Code § 78a.65 (a)(1).
Violation ID: 8167838
Permit API: 125-28290
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Carroll Township
Inspection Type: Site Restoration
Inspection Date: 12/06/2023
Comments: On 12/06/2023, a post drilling restoration inspection was conducted for the Harold Haywood 26H well. The Department received the post drilling restoration report on 12/01/2023. EQT employee onsite. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance (Photo 1).The 26H well was in generally good condition and equipped with a well tag displaying the permit number and the operator's information (Photos 2-4). Some water in cellar. The 26H GPU appeared in generally good condition and containment noted. The production tanks were also in containment (Photos 5-8). Box tank onsite in containment - I asked employee onsite about this and it is no longer in use from the sand traps. Some corrosion on piping (Photos 9, 10).There was no drilling equipment on site (Photos 11-14).Some sediment at beginning of access road leading towards main road. I recommend that this is addressed (Photos 15, 16)The drilling, well completion, and stimulation completion dates for the 26H well were 05/20/2019 (drill), 05/25/2023 (well completed), and 08/12/2019 (stimulations). The operator submitted the post drilling well site restoration report on 12/01/2023. Due to the delay in submission, a violation of 78a.65(e) is being noted and immediately corrected. I recommend that the post drilling restoration report is approved.

Violation ID: 924728
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/27/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of an estimated 5 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the pad surface on Pad B. This inspection was only conducted on Pad B. I met with EQT Company Man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release which was along the edge of the well site secondary containment in the travel lane near the company man trailer. The area had already been scraped and backfilled at the time of this inspection. The company man said that the release had occurred from a radiator on a cement truck that was offloading into the upright cement tanks at the time. The truck was straddling the edge of the well site secondary containment so the fluid leaked onto the pad surface. The cement trucks were moved onto the secondary containment as of this inspection. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected. The sump that is in place on the opposite side of the pad surface has had a metal lid placed on it. This sump was installed after fluid with elevated conductivity was discovered by the Department in that area of the pad. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the sump was approximately 1350 uS/cm. The area around the sump on the pad surface was dry during this inspection. Violations remain outstanding in association with this release.

Comments: On October 2, 2025, the Department conducted a Routine Complete Inspection of K Petroleum Inc's Patterson 1 well site located in Nottingham Township, Washington County.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag with all required information posted on it fixed to the wellhead on site. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a meter box and separator on site. The meter box was observed to have a well posting fixed to it with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this meter box and separator.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a production tank within an earthen dike. An approximately 6 ft by 4 ft area on the ground at the base of the production tank where the valve is located was observed to be lacking vegetative cover. Pieces of the valve appeared to be broken off and was observed to be laying on the ground adjacent to the production tank. At the time of this inspection, an orange sheeny substance was observed to be actively dripping from the valve onto the ground around the production tank. The ground in this area was observed to be stained a dark black color with pooling of the orange substance observed directly below the valve. At the time of this inspection the Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the ground in this release area. Soil conductivity readings of 0.460 mS, 0.237 mS, 0.329 mS, and 0.308 mS were collected and compared to a background soil conductivity readings of 0.0635 mS collected in a vegetated area adjacent to the well site. These soil conductivity readings are elevated when compared to the background soil conductivity reading, which further subjugates that a release has occurred in this area. While on site, the Department called the number listed on the well tag/well posting as well as K Petroleum Inc's Robert Inghram. The Department was not able to reach either via phone, therefore the Department left a voicemail for each regarding the findings during today's inspection.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based one today's inspection, violations are being issued for a release from the production tank.

Inspection Date: 7/07/2022
Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to review operator response to NOV associated with inspection report # 3373528. Weather conditions at time of inspection are sunny and 81 degrees F. Meeting on site today with Cole Maxwell, Area Water Coordinator with Balackhill Energy and Kyle Jackson, Environmental Technician with Moody's Environmental. During this inspection an Elk Environmental Services water truck is removing produced fluid from vertical tanks at northeast corner of pad. Areas across the well pad have been scraped and excavated to remove soils contaminated with regulated substances. An equipment operator with Fenton Transport is operating a skid-steer with loader bucket, an excavator and a mini-excavator to remove impacted soils. 22 steel bins are located on site along with 3 vacuum boxes for vacuuming up puddles following precipitation events. Areas of the pad that have been scraped or dug for removal include soils around well cellars and a large area of the eastern section of the pad toward the produced fluid tanks and where evaporator concentrated fluid secondary containment was located. Test pits and shallow trenches have been dug near the east and west sides of the well cellars. According to Mr. Maxwell, the limiting factor for the cleanup operation is the hauling and return of empty bins for contaminated soils. A Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity probe and organic free reagent water were used to screen for conductivity on the pad. Areas to the east and west of well cellars and between GPUs and produced fluid containment continue to show elevated conductivity (photos 3 and 5). These areas were pointed out to Mr Maxwell and Jackson and are expected to be scraped as disposal bins become available. Cleanup activity is expected to continue until soil screenings indicate conductivity levels under 1 mS/cm.There are no new violations at this time.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/22/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8169388
Permit API: 081-21908
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/22/2023
Comments: On December 22, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the EQT ARO LLC Salt Run Hunting Club Pad A Extension. EQT reported a spill of approximately 300 gallons of glycol outside of containment and onto the well pad surface on the morning of December 22, 2023. Upon arrival, DEP spoke with EQT Rick Hall and he said that a valve fitting failed on one of the dehydration units. This caused glycol to mist onto the well pad surface. The area of impact was about 60 feet by 60 feet, in an "L" shape due to the dehydration equipment being in place. The depth of the impact to the well pad surface was unknown at the time of the inspection. Excavation of the area had not begun while DEP was onsite. EQT was waiting on equipment to be delivered to the well pad to begin the excavation around the dehydration unit and gas lines. A plan was still being developed by EQT to clean off the equipment that the glycol came in contact with. EQT plans to have Penn E and R begin the Act 2 remediation process. DEP spoke with Mr. Hall on December 26, 2023. The equipment that the glycol came in contact with was washed down. Mr. Hall said that the excavation of the impacted area was completed late on December 22, 2023. Confirmatory samples were collected and Mr. Hall provided DEP with pictures of the excavated area. The spill of glycol outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.56(a).

Violation ID: 8287676
Permit API: 051-22973
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/31/2026
Comments: On 8/31/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Orr 14 OG well in Washington Township, Fayette County. This inspection follows-up to IR 4266621, where violations were issued for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures prior to conducting earth disturbances on the access road, which is resulting in a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth. Diversified representative Jared Walker was present on site during this inspection.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The access road appears to be a multi-use road that is shared with additional Diversified well sites. Some tire rutting was observed in the shared access road. No Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the access road entrance. Step 1.3 of the E and S/Restoration plan construction sequence is to install a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) at the access road entrance prior to conducting earth disturbances.- The well site is located within a forested agricultural area. Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed downslope of the well site. Portions of the compost filter sock are holding minor amounts of sediment. In other portions of the CFS, the stakes appear to be dislodged. This does not appear to be affecting the functionality of the CFS at the time of inspection. However, the Department recommends that the Operator conduct maintenance on the CFS. Violations may be forthcoming pending re-evaluation of this location in a future inspection. Rig mats are being installed on the saturated ground around the gas well. The E and S/Restoration plan and a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) are located at the Navaho Hollow Road entrance, which will not be used for well plugging operations. The E and S/Restoration plan is not specific to the Connellsville Street access road, which is being used for plugging operations. - The gas well is equipped with a well tag. A plugging rig and well plugging equipment have been staged on site. Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/07/2023
Comments: On March 7, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Bozich 2 well in North Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3482092 where it was found that although contaminated soil was removed from the point of impact, contamination from the stockpile was found to be leaching into the soil downslope. Recurring violations were issued as a result. The operator then explained that the tarp which was used to cover it must have been removed by inclement weather, and then proceeded to cover it with reinforced tarp and surround it with straw and silt fence. This was discussed via phone in IR 3483449. As of the date of this Admin inspection, the operator is waiting for the ground to either freeze or thaw enough for machinery to access the well site and remove the excavation stockpile. Kriebel representative Shane Kriebel roughly estimates that 20-25 gallons of fluid escaped from the tank before Kriebel acquired the well site.The following was observed:Heavy tire rutting was observed in the access road leading to the well site (see photo 1). The well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns related to E and S or vegetative coverage (see photos 2 and 3). It was temporarily stabilized and appeared to be establishing vegetation. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the well head (see photo 4), and it was equipped with a well tag (see photo 5). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the formerly impacted areas around the brine tank, which appeared to be comparable to that of the surrounding soil (see photos 6-8). Additional conductivity readings were taken where contamination from the excavation stockpile was found in IR 3482092 (see photos 9-11). Elevated conductivity was found within 2 feet downslope of the stockpile. A background soil conductivity reading was taken in the crop field east of the well site, which read 230 Microsiemens (see photo 12).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that the point of impact has been remediated and is now recovering. However, contamination from the excavation stockpile may still be impacting the soil downslope, although it does not appear to be spreading. Therefore, closure of violations shall be contingent upon submittal of waste manifest to the Department; removal and proper disposal of the excavation stockpile, and any additional impacted soil discovered underneath or downslope; and a subsequent CEI inspection. Violations remain outstanding.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 984604
Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/06/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification received on February 3, 2023 from the operator of a release of produced fluid to the pad surface and access road of Pad B from clam boxes which were being removed from the location. Two snubbing units are in operation on Pad B. I met with company man Josh Scheihing upon arriving on Pad B. He showed me where on the access road the release had occurred. The surface had already been scraped at the time of this inspection. No fluid was observed in this area. Some clam shell boxes were present along the access road near the area that had been scraped. According to the operator, these boxes were empty and were slated to be removed. I walked the rest of the site with the company man. The fluid in the sump at the northeast stormwater channel outlet was frozen. There was snow and ice present in the northeast corner of the pad but no fluid was observed. The majority of the pad surface was dry or had snow and ice on it. I found an area along the east side of the pad with fluid with an electrical conductivity (EC) of greater than 19.99 mS/cm near a trailer for MidAtlantic Energy Services. The farther away from the trailer I took EC readings, the more the EC decreased. At the farthest north point of the fluid puddle, the EC was 1977 uS/cm and at the farther point to the south the EC was 2.74 mS/cm. I took sample 0718-203 from the area next to the MidAtlantic Energy Services trailer to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. I let the company man know what I found before leaving the location. I called Rick Hall of EQT on the same day after leaving the location to let him know what I found. On the same day, Zac Subra of EQT sent me an email which stated that they had done their own investigation on the pad and had found out that MidAtlantic Energy Services used ice melt to melt the ice around their trailer. EQT believes that this caused the elevated electrical conductivity. The email included photos of the ice melt used. Also on the same day the operator notified the Department that fluid with a high electrical conductivity was found beneath rig mats on the pad. The notification stated that the operator believed that this fluid may be associated with the release from the clam shell boxes which occurred on 2/3/23 since the clam shells had been stored on the dancefloor prior to being moved off of the pad. The operator estimated the volume of this fluid at 42 gallons. Due to the estimated volume of the release, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation for this release.Violations noted for the release from the clam shell boxes to Pad B and the Pad B access road.

properties.content:

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 904088
Permit API: 003-22470
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Forward Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/05/2021
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to an operator reported spill. The incident was reported to the Department at approximately 6:33PM on 12/23/2020. Mr. Hardy from EQT was spoken to by phone on 12/24/2020. According to Mr. Hardy, the incident occurred at approximately 4:30PM on 12/23/2020. According to Mr. Hardy a pipe inside the GPU housing leaked, with approximately 5-10 gallons of fluid impacting the ground. The operator contacted SPSI to remediate. According to an email received from Mr. Hardy later in the day, impacted water was seeping from underneath the GPU into an excavated ditch. The operator has left the ditch open to act as a sump and the water will be vacuumed out as necessary. Per the operator, remediation is being conducted in accordance with 78a.66c(1), in reference to spills or releases less than 42 gallons. Based on that, the Department recommends that the operator fully remediate the site in accordance with 91.33(B), otherwise the Department requests that the operator reevaluate how much fluid was lost. Pictures taken by the operator have been attached to this inspection (Photo 1-6). Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the discharge to the ground. The Department will schedule an on-site visit to follow up with the remediation effort as soon as possible. Pending the operator's response and the follow up inspection, further violations may be issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/30/2023 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Terry Twp, Bradford county. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/30/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 990005
Permit API: 015-23753
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Terry Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/30/2023
Comments: On 3/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 25 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. Water/ice puddles from recent rain/snowfall were scattered across the pad surface. I field tested some of these with an Oakton PCTS 50 for conductivity and discovered a 60' x 60' ice/water puddle southeast of the wellheads and adjacent to the south edge of the secondary containment for six frac tanks that field tested at 4.05 mS conductance. Sample 9551-049 was collected from this puddle. Two water puddles between the two frac tank secondary containments field tested at 1.5 mS conductance. Other water puddles tested at less than 0.6 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance fluids with Chesapeake's Kyle Stephens. He directed an arriving vac truck to start sucking up the fluids. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization has been applied to the perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. Temporary compost filter socks remain in place down slope from the infiltration areas.There were five wells staged for flowback/production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks in secondary containment that were connected to the wellheads. There were 10 frac tanks on the north side of location that were stationed in secondary containment but were not connected to the well heads at the time of the inspection.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3517519 for high conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface while cleaning up after fracking operations were completed and for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.The release of a large volume of elevated conductance fluid to the unprotected pad surface is a violation of CSL 402[b)The DEP recommends the following:1. Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.2. Continue to monitor the areas with temporary stabilization and apply addition resources as necessary to achieve at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation.I left the site at 1010 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/18/2021 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/18/2021
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 933605
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/18/2021
Comments: Site inspection conducted to review residual waste processing activities at the EQT COP 551B pad with EQT Company Man Bill Mitchell. Weather at time of inspection is partly sunny and 46 degrees F. According to Mr. Mitchell, Precision Drilling Rig #110 is currently drilling the 6H well at a depth of 6378'. This is the 7th well of 9 total to be drilled during this setup. Drilling resumed on the 6H well on 10/15 and the well is being drilled using Water Based Mud to kickoff point at 8650' where the rig will be switched over to Synthetic OBM. The anticipated Total Depth of the 6H well is 22897'. All nine wells have been batch drilled to the intermediate depth. The 7H well was recently completed and cemented on 10/13. Clean Harbors Backyard Crew is processing the drill cuttings in the rig backyard. Three shale shakers and three drying shakers are active. Polymer flocculant is being added to the drilling mud during this inspection before it is run through the centrifuge. One centrifuge is removing cuttings from the drilling mud. An excavator is mixing wood pellets into the drill cuttings to solidify the material for landfill disposal. Prior to site transfer to EQT, ARD submitted a Request for Approval for Previously Approved Alternative Waste Management Practices (OG71) Form B for this well pad on 2/2/2021. The Department approved the request on 2/3/2021. The intent of onsite drill cuttings processing is to separate the solid fraction of the cuttings from reusable drilling mud fluid so fluids can be returned to mud tanks for further drilling activity. For further information, refer to the COP Tract 357 Pad A OG-71 Form A application regarding drill cuttings processing (EFACTS authorization #1300435). During this inspection, fluid with a sheen is observed within tertiary containment outside the OBM tanks. The Department recommends that containment structures be vacuumed and fluids be sent for treatment or disposal. The original trench sump collecting runoff along the access road near the mud tanks has a field conductivity reading of 733 uS/cm. There Re no new violations noted during this inspection. Violations remain outstanding on Pad B based on Inspection Report #3231577 by DEP WQS Brad Kline dated 8/9/21.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8168031
Permit API: 065-25518
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Knox Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2023
Comments: This site located west off Odonnell Road, 1 1/2 miles south of railroad crossing on State Game Lands Road, at the end of second branch to the north. Well is set-up for production with a meter, separator and one tank in secondary containment. Tank has been removed from site. A report of a release of 32 gallons of produced water was reported by Will Warfel with Diversified Prod LLC at 12:30 on 9/21/23 at this well site. The release was assumed to be from the separator, there is an area of no vegetation around the well head, separator and meter and a path 70x15' path to the west. WQS Taylor received notification from Heather Empfield that Moody and Associates Inc were to be employed to sample this site to determine the extent of the contamination. Contaminated soil has been removed from end of path of dead vegetation to the west. Based on conductivity testing, completed on October 24, 2023 at an onsite meeting with Lisa Raffle, Wil Warfel and Paul Stiner, there is brine contaminated soil near the well head and secondary containment around the tank, on the stabilized parking area and in all areas of dead vegetation from the original notification of a release on site. Stone has been placed on the initial uphill section of the access road, partial stabilization has been completed. Access is still muddy and rutted, should be stabilized. This well is on Exhibit A of the Diversified Consent Order and Agreement and shows no annual production.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 997796
Permit API: 015-23689
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2023
Comments: On 6/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Solowiej well site. It was 65 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. I did not screen for conductivity because I did not witness any water puddles or muddy areas on the pad surface during the inspection.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by one sediment pond. The sediment pond is adequately stabilized and was dry at the time of the inspection. I was able to witness an 8 inch riser sticking up about 16 inches from the pond surface. The outlet for the sediment pond overflow drains into a stream alongside the River View roadway. This stream drains to the waters of the Commonwealth. Following an inspection conducted on 10/18/2022, Chesapeake reported that it would make changes to the site to mitigate the issues with the sediment pond. They reported that they were developing a design to accommodate both the drainage and the land owner and hoped to have a finalized plan with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features. There are outstanding violations against the outfall coming off the sediment pond. There were three wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment.The DEP recommends that Chesapeake continues with the process to obtain a revised ESCGP application with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features and submit to the Department for review.I left the site at 1400 hours.

Report Details

Violation Date: 10/23/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8205474
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 10/23/2024
Comments: On 10/23/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of three water samples that were collected during fracking operations from three different locations at the site. During inspections #3846615 and #3846665, conducted on 10/2/2024 and 10/3/2024; the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad. Samples were collected on 10/3/2024. On 10/19/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Sample 9551-142 was collected from the south of two puddles of water near the outfall at the center of the north perimeter berm; both puddles field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. The upper limit for conductivity on the Altair PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. The south puddle measured 6' x 1.5' x 3 inches and the north puddle measured 10' x 3' x 2". The 16" freshwater pipeline and the 16" frac water pipeline traveled through these puddles. There was a multi-colored crusty sheen and the water left a brown film on the sample bottles. The results are shown in pictures 1-3.Sample 9551-143 was collected from within MRC basin 1 in a water/muddy area where the outfall from the center of the north perimeter berm flows into the basin. Water in this area field tested at 16.92 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 4-6. Sample 9551-144 was collected from within MRC basin 1, next to the east basin overflow. Water in this area field tested at 1.595 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 7-8.The samples show elevated levels of aluminum, iron, manganese, chlorides and strontium which indicates the release of a pollutional substance on the pad and reaching the basin.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2). This incident does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b). Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the elevated conductance, aluminum, iron, manganese, strontium and chlorides in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

Report Details
Inspection Client: D & B GAS PROD LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 1/26/2024
Violation Code: 78.88(a) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to inspect each operating well quarterly for compliance with the well construction and operating requirements.
Violation ID: 8173920
Permit API: 129-24015
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: North Huntingdon Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/26/2024
Comments: On 1/26/24 an on site inspection was conducted by OGI Matt Woods in response to WQS referral. The findings of the inspection are listed below. - Well is currently in production. - APR has been submitted for 2023. -MIA has not been submitted since 2021 for year 2020. Due to failure to submit the following violations are being cited. 78.88(a), 78.88(b)1-4 and 78,88(e). - Past inspection noted possible leaks on equipment, OGI was unable to hear any hissing coming from equipment during inspection. - On 12/13/22 WQS Adam Clark had a phone conversation with D and B rep Brian Bittinger to discuss the issues he found at the site and confirm receipt of inspection #3446428. During the phone call the issue that no fence was in place to protect the well from the longhorn steers was discussed. The steers are able to rub against the equipment and cause damage to the equipment. The rep stated that they plan to place a fence around the well. At this time no fence is in place to protect the equipment. DEP request information on when the fence will be constructed.
